results.reasoning: Re-judge of the n-0131 fail. Drove node bin/walkdown.js where live under a scratch WALKDOWN_HOME against eleven arranged situations - a bare git repo with nothing, an in-tree blueprint whose runs/ exists while threads/ does not, a config-named project whose spec sits outside any repository with a per-kind evidence override, a config-named spec sitting in a different git repository from the roots-named code repo, a plain no-git directory, --dir from an unrelated cwd and --dir across repositories, a defaults: block with {id}, an unparseable config, a legacy projects/<id>/ home, the single-kind scripts form - plus the real project's own answer with the real home. Every row of every answer carries a reason, the reasons name the deciding rule rather than that a decision was made ('named on the command line', 'this machine's config (<id>)', 'the config default', 'already in the blueprint', 'found in the working tree', 'beside the spec, as runs and threads follow it', 'the built-in default, outside the repository (allocated on first write)', with the legacy-home variant naming the migrate remedy), the config line reports its own state including the parse error verbatim, and --json carries the same why strings. The code row, n-0131's defect, now distinguishes its three situations truthfully: 'the git repository the spec sits in' only when that is true (in-tree, cross-repo), 'the working directory's repository - the spec sits outside any repository' in the fresh-adopter shape that used to be mislabeled, and 'no git repository - runs will carry no git_sha' with no path at all when there is none. I could not make any row misname its decision; a mixed answer (probe C: flag-less config spec, followed runs/threads, overridden evidence, defaulted drafts) names four different decisions on one screen, which is exactly the statement's point. Same reading as the prior judge on the scripts form: where <kind> prints a bare path and the rule governs the report. One adjacent tension found while verifying the D code row against the recorder is a provenance question, not a says-why one - the row honestly reports the resolver's choice - filed separately as n-0134.
